Maladaptive Strategies.value: try hard not think about the trauma
Going out at night or being outside after dark
Any form of physical contact with others

Memory.value: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette:
Adebayo was, at nineteen, the youngest detective in his precinct, a fact he had carried with immense pride until three months ago. Now, that pride feels like a memory from someone else’s life. His career, and his sense of self, began to unravel in the damp darkness of a warehouse basement where he was held for forty-eight hours after an undercover assignment went disastrously wrong. He was supposed to be observing a trafficking ring, but he was identified, grabbed from a darkened alley, and thrown into a windowless room. He remembers the scratch of the burlap sack over his head, the cold bite of zip ties on his wrists, and the low, indistinct murmur of his captors’ voices from the other side of a heavy steel door.

The event itself remains a blur, a collection of terrifying fragments rather than a coherent narrative. Adebayo struggles to articulate the experience, even to himself. He tells his therapist he knows what happened, that he can list the sequence of events, but when he tries to describe the feeling of it, he is unable to find the words. The memory doesn't live in his mind as a story. Instead, it lives in his ears. While trying to complete paperwork at his desk, he will suddenly hear the sharp, metallic click of the bolt sliding shut on that basement door, a sound so vivid he flinches, expecting to find himself back in the dark. At other times, a wave of pure, sickening terror will wash over him without warning or context. There is no image attached, just the raw, physical sensation of helplessness and dread he felt while tied to a chair, leaving him breathless and disoriented in the middle of his own kitchen.

These intrusive, fragmented memories have become the central threat in Adebayo’s life, and his days are now organized around a desperate effort to control them. The auditory flashbacks and surges of emotion are so unpredictable and overpowering that his primary response is to try to force them out of his mind. He spends hours trying hard not to think about the trauma, a constant, exhausting battle of mental suppression that only seems to make the intrusions more frequent. Because the terror is so strongly associated with the blackness of the basement, he has come to see all darkness as dangerous. He no longer takes night shifts, a significant problem for a detective, and refuses to leave his apartment after sunset, cutting himself off from friends and social events. The memory of being restrained has poisoned all physical contact. When his girlfriend, Imani, reaches out to comfort him, he recoils instinctively, the gentle touch of her hand feeling like the prelude to being bound. He sees the hurt and confusion in her eyes but feels powerless to stop the reaction.

The strategies he adopted for survival are now dismantling his life. His avoidance of night duty has drawn concerned questions from his supervising officer, threatening the career he worked so hard to build. His relationship with Imani is fraying under the strain of his withdrawal and his inability to accept or offer physical affection. He feels trapped in a shrinking world, policed by the echoes of what happened in that basement. He finally sought help after Imani found him one night standing rigidly in the living room, every light in the apartment blazing. He had been woken by the sound of the refrigerator’s compressor kicking on, his mind instantly translating it into the hum of the warehouse’s faulty generator. He is here because he is terrified of losing everything that once defined him—his job, his relationship, his own sense of safety—to a memory he can neither fully recall nor ever seem to escape.
